source.text: וַֽעֲתַלְיָה֙ אֵ֣ם אֲחַזְיָ֔הוּ רָאֲתָ֖ה כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת בְּנָ֑הּ וַתָּ֨קָם֙ וַתְּאַבֵּ֔ד אֵ֖ת כָּל־זֶ֥רַע הַמַּמְלָכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Athaliah, mother of Ahaziah, saw that dead [was] her son, and arose and destroyed all [the] offspring of the kingdom.

en.L: And Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son [was] dead, and she arose and destroyed all the offspring of the kingdom.
en.B: Athaliah, Ahaziah's mother, saw that her son was dead, and she set out to destroy the whole royal family.
en.R: Ahaziah's mother Athaliah saw that her son was dead. So she started killing everyone in the royal family.

decisions.choice: Athaliah: the queen mother, of the house of Ahab
decisions.reason: Athaliah was a daughter of Ahab's house (8:18, 26) and the mother of Ahaziah king of Judah. Ahaziah had been killed by Jehu's men (9:27). With her son dead, she seized the throne herself.

decisions.choice: the offspring of the kingdom: the royal family, everyone with a claim to the throne
decisions.reason: The phrase means the king's descendants, the line from which the next king would come. Many of Ahaziah's relatives had already been killed by Jehu (10:13-14); Athaliah now kills the rest she can find.

decisions.choice: arose and destroyed: she set about killing them
decisions.reason: "Arose" marks the start of a deliberate action. The verse says what she set out to do; verse 2 shows that one child escaped.

decisions.choice: saw
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew and the traditional reading notes differ here by one letter (with or without "and" before "saw"). The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: 2 Chronicles 22:10-23:21 retells this story
decisions.reason: Chronicles tells the same events in nearly the same words, with some differences: it says that Jehosheba was Jehoiada's wife (2 Chronicles 22:11), and it gives a large part to the Levites and the assembly where Kings speaks of the Carites and the guards. The differences are noted at the verses where they occur.

decisions.choice: set out to destroy (Balanced); started killing (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that she began the killing but did not finish it (verse 2).

source.text: וַתִּקַּ֣ח יְהוֹשֶׁ֣בַע בַּת־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־י֠וֹרָם אֲח֨וֹת אֲחַזְיָ֜הוּ אֶת־יוֹאָ֣שׁ בֶּן־אֲחַזְיָ֗ה וַתִּגְנֹ֤ב אֹתוֹ֙ מִתּ֤וֹךְ בְּנֵֽי־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַמּ֣וּמָתִ֔ים אֹת֥וֹ וְאֶת־מֵינִקְתּ֖וֹ בַּחֲדַ֣ר הַמִּטּ֑וֹת וַיַּסְתִּ֧רוּ אֹת֛וֹ מִפְּנֵ֥י עֲתַלְיָ֖הוּ וְלֹ֥א הוּמָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Jehosheba, daughter of the king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, Joash son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among [the] sons of the king who [were] being put to death, him and his nurse, in [the] room of the beds; and they hid him from before Athaliah, and not he was put to death.

en.L: And Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, the sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the sons of the king who were being put to death, [and put] him and his nurse in the room of the beds; and they hid him from Athaliah, and he was not put to death.
en.B: But Jehosheba, King Joram's daughter and Ahaziah's sister, took Ahaziah's son Joash and secretly took him out from among the king's sons who were about to be killed. She put him and his nurse in the bedroom, and they hid him from Athaliah, so he was not killed.
en.R: But Jehosheba, who was King Joram's daughter and Ahaziah's sister, took Ahaziah's son Joash. The king's sons were about to be killed, but she secretly took him away from among them. She put him and his nurse in a bedroom. So they kept him hidden from Athaliah, and he was not killed.

decisions.choice: Jehosheba: the king's daughter and the dead king's sister
decisions.reason: Jehosheba was a daughter of King Joram of Judah and so the sister, or half-sister, of Ahaziah. The text does not say whether Athaliah was her mother. 2 Chronicles 22:11 adds that she was the wife of Jehoiada the priest, which explains how the child could be hidden in the temple (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the room of the beds: a bedroom
alternatives: a storeroom for beds and bedding
decisions.reason: The phrase means a room for beds. It may be a bedroom in the palace or the temple buildings, or a storeroom where beds and bedding were kept. Either way it was a place where a small child and his nurse could be kept out of sight.

decisions.choice: him and his nurse: the verb for putting them in the room is understood
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names Joash and his nurse and the room but gives no verb for putting them there. 2 Chronicles 22:11, which tells the same event, has "and she put him and his nurse in the room of the beds".

decisions.choice: they hid him: Jehosheba and the nurse
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. It most likely means Jehosheba and the nurse together; 2 Chronicles 22:11 has "she hid him".

decisions.choice: who were being put to death: the killing was under way
decisions.reason: The form describes the king's sons as in the process of being killed. Jehosheba took the child out from among them before he could be found.

decisions.choice: [and put]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the missing verb in brackets (m3).

decisions.choice: the bedroom (Balanced); a bedroom (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday word for a room for beds; the footnote on m2 gives the other possible sense.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י אִתָּהּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה מִתְחַבֵּ֖א שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים וַעֲתַלְיָ֖ה מֹלֶ֥כֶת עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he was with her [in the] house of Yahweh hiding himself six years, and Athaliah [was] reigning over the land.

en.L: And he was with her [in] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, hiding, six years, while Athaliah was reigning over the land.
en.B: He stayed hidden with her in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} six years, during Athaliah's rule over the land.
en.R: For six years Joash stayed hidden with Jehosheba in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, while Athaliah ruled the country as queen.

decisions.choice: with her: with Jehosheba
decisions.reason: "Her" most naturally means Jehosheba, who rescued him (verse 2); it could also mean the nurse, who was hidden with him.

decisions.choice: the house of Yahweh: the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The child was hidden in the temple buildings, where Jehoiada the priest served (verse 4). The temple had many side rooms (1 Kings 6:5).

decisions.choice: Athaliah was reigning: the only woman to rule as monarch in Judah or Israel
decisions.reason: Athaliah held the throne for six years. Unlike every king of Judah and Israel, her reign has no opening or closing formula in Kings, and no one is said to reign after her until Joash.

decisions.choice: Joash; Jehosheba; as queen
decisions.reason: Readable names the people the pronouns refer to (m1) and says that Athaliah ruled as queen.

source.text: וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠שְּׁבִיעִית שָׁלַ֨ח יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע וַיִּקַּ֣ח׀אֶת־שָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֗וֹת לַכָּרִי֙ וְלָ֣רָצִ֔ים וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֛ם אֵלָ֖יו בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּכְרֹת֩ לָהֶ֨ם בְּרִ֜ית וַיַּשְׁבַּ֤ע אֹתָם֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֥רְא אֹתָ֖ם אֶת־בֶּן־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And in the year the seventh sent Jehoiada and took the commanders of the hundreds of the Carites and of the runners, and brought them to him [to the] house of Yahweh; and cut to them a covenant and made swear them in [the] house of Yahweh, and showed them the son of the king.

en.L: And in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the runners, and he brought them to himself [into] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and he made a covenant with them and made them swear in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he showed them the son of the king.
en.B: In the seventh year Jehoiada sent for the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the guards and had them brought to him in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then he showed them the king's son.
en.R: In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest sent for the commanders of the Carites and of the palace guards, each of whom led a hundred men. He had them come to him in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. There he made a covenant with them and had them swear an oath. Then he showed them the king's son.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada: the priest at the temple
decisions.reason: Jehoiada is called "the priest" from verse 9 on. 2 Chronicles 22:11 says he was Jehosheba's husband (verse 2).

decisions.choice: the Carites: a unit of the royal guard, perhaps foreign soldiers
decisions.reason: The name appears only here, in verse 19 and in the written text of 2 Samuel 20:23. It may refer to soldiers hired from Caria, a land in the southwest of Asia Minor whose men served as soldiers abroad, or it may be another form of the name "Cherethites", David's foreign guard (2 Samuel 8:18; 1 Kings 1:38). Either way they were part of the king's guard. 2 Chronicles 23:1-2 does not name them and speaks instead of the Levites and the heads of families.

decisions.choice: the runners: the king's guard
decisions.reason: The "runners" were royal guards who ran before the king's chariot and kept watch at his palace (1 Kings 14:27-28).

decisions.choice: commanders of hundreds: officers each over a unit of about a hundred men
decisions.reason: The army and the guard were organized in units of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens (1 Samuel 22:7; Exodus 18:21).

decisions.choice: made a covenant with them and made them swear: a sworn agreement
decisions.reason: Jehoiada bound the officers to himself by an oath taken in the temple, before Yahweh, before he risked showing them the hidden prince.

decisions.choice: the guards (Balanced); the palace guards (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 14:27, Balanced and Readable name what the runners were (m3).

decisions.choice: the priest; each of whom led a hundred men
decisions.reason: Readable says who Jehoiada was (verse 9) and explains "commanders of hundreds".

source.text: וַיְצַוֵּ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּן הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֤ית מִכֶּם֙ בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת וְשֹׁ֣מְרֵ֔י מִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he commanded them, saying, This [is] the thing which you will do: the third of you, [those] coming in [on] the sabbath and keepers of [the] watch of [the] house of the king,

en.L: And he commanded them, saying, "This [is] the thing that you shall do: the third of you who come in on the sabbath [shall be] keepers of the watch of the house of the king,
en.B: He gave them this order: "Here is what you must do. One third of you, the men who come on duty on the sabbath, will keep watch over the king's palace,
en.R: He gave them these orders: "Here is what you must do. The men who come on duty on the sabbath will be divided into three groups. One group will guard the king's palace.

decisions.choice: coming in on the sabbath: coming on duty when the guard changed
alternatives: those who came to the temple on the sabbath
decisions.reason: The guard served in shifts that changed on the sabbath. Those "coming in" began their duty that day; those "going out" (verses 7 and 9) ended theirs. On that day both groups were in the city at once, which gave Jehoiada a double force without raising suspicion.

decisions.choice: the third of you: the men coming on duty are divided into three groups
alternatives: a third of you who come on duty, and those who keep watch over the palace
decisions.reason: Verses 5-7 are hard to follow in Hebrew. The most likely reading is that the men coming on duty are split into three parts, one at the palace and one at each of two gates (verse 6), while the two companies going off duty guard the temple and the king (verse 7). The "and" before "keepers" may instead join two groups, so that the verse describes more units than three.

decisions.choice: the house of the king: the palace
decisions.reason: The palace stood beside the temple, close enough that Athaliah could hear the noise (verse 13).

decisions.choice: will be divided into three groups. One group
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the division into three that verses 5-6 imply (m2).

source.text: וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁית֙ בְּשַׁ֣עַר ס֔וּר וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁ֥ית בַּשַּׁ֖עַר אַחַ֣ר הָרָצִ֑ים וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֛ם אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת הַבַּ֖יִת מַסָּֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: and the third at [the] gate of Sur, and the third at the gate behind the runners; and you will keep [the] watch of the house, by turns.

en.L: and the third at the gate of Sur, and the third at the gate behind the runners; and you shall keep the watch of the house by turns.
en.B: one third at the Sur Gate, and one third at the gate behind the guards. So you will guard the palace in turns.
en.R: Another group will be at the Sur Gate, and the third group at the gate behind the guards. In this way you will take turns guarding the palace.

decisions.choice: the gate of Sur: a gate of the palace or temple whose site is unknown
decisions.reason: This gate is not named anywhere else. 2 Chronicles 23:5 has "the gate of the Foundation" instead, which in Hebrew differs from "Sur" by little more than one letter.

decisions.choice: the gate behind the runners: probably the guards' gate into the palace
decisions.reason: Verse 19 speaks of "the gate of the runners" leading from the temple to the palace; this is probably the same gate, near the guards' quarters.

decisions.choice: by turns: in shifts
decisions.reason: The last word of the verse appears nowhere else, and its sense is a guess from context. It may mean "in turns", "as a barrier" (keeping people away), or it may be a place name.

decisions.choice: the house: the palace
decisions.reason: After verse 5, "the house" here most likely means the king's house, the palace, rather than the temple, which is named separately in verse 7.

source.text: וּשְׁתֵּ֤י הַיָּדוֹת֙ בָּכֶ֔ם כֹּ֖ל יֹצְאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וְשָֽׁמְר֛וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] two of the hands among you, all [those] going out [on] the sabbath, and they will keep [the] watch of [the] house of Yahweh for the king.

en.L: And the two divisions among you, all who go out on the sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for the king.
en.B: The two companies of you who go off duty on the sabbath are all to keep watch over the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to protect the king.
en.R: Your other two groups, the men who finish their duty on the sabbath, must all guard the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to protect the king.

decisions.choice: the two hands: two divisions or companies
decisions.reason: "Hand" here means a part or share (Genesis 47:24). The guard was made up of companies, and two of them were going off duty.

decisions.choice: going out on the sabbath: going off duty
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. Those going off duty did not go home but were kept at the temple.

decisions.choice: for the king: to protect the king
decisions.reason: Their task in the temple was to guard the young king when he was brought out (verse 8).

decisions.choice: Your other two groups
decisions.reason: Readable adds "other" to show that these are different from the three groups of verses 5-6, following the reading in the decision at verse 5.

source.text: וְהִקַּפְתֶּ֨ם עַל־הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ סָבִ֗יב אִ֚ישׁ וְכֵלָ֣יו בְּיָד֔וֹ וְהַבָּ֥א אֶל־הַשְּׂדֵר֖וֹת יוּמָ֑ת וִהְי֥וּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּצֵאת֥וֹ וּבְבֹאֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will surround the king all around, each man and his weapons in his hand, and the [one] coming into the ranks will be put to death; and be with the king in his going out and in his coming in.

en.L: And you shall surround the king all around, each man with his weapons in his hand, and whoever comes into the ranks shall be put to death; and be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in."
en.B: Surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in hand. Anyone who comes within your ranks must be put to death. Stay with the king wherever he goes."
en.R: Form a circle around the king, every man holding his weapons. Anyone who comes inside your lines must be killed. Stay close to the king wherever he goes."

decisions.choice: the ranks: the lines of guards
decisions.reason: The word means rows or ranks. Here it most likely means the lines the guards formed around the king, so that anyone pushing into them was an attacker. It is used again in verse 15.

decisions.choice: when he goes out and when he comes in: wherever he goes
decisions.reason: Going out and coming in together cover all of a person's movements (Deuteronomy 28:6; 1 Samuel 18:16).

decisions.choice: the orders end here
decisions.reason: Jehoiada's orders that began in verse 5 end with this verse; verse 9 tells how they were carried out.

decisions.choice: wherever he goes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m2).

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֞וּ שָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֗וֹת כְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּה֮ יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע הַכֹּהֵן֒ וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־אֲנָשָׁ֔יו בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת עִ֖ם יֹצְאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־יְהוֹיָדָ֥ע הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And did [the] commanders of the hundreds according to all that commanded Jehoiada the priest, and took each his men, [those] coming in [on] the sabbath with [those] going out [on] the sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.

en.L: And the commanders of hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest had commanded, and each took his men, those coming in on the sabbath with those going out on the sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
en.B: The commanders of hundreds did everything Jehoiada the priest had ordered. Each brought his men, both the ones who came on duty on the sabbath and the ones who went off duty that day, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
en.R: The commanders did just what Jehoiada the priest told them. Each one brought his men, both those who were starting their duty on the sabbath and those who were finishing it. They all came to Jehoiada the priest.

decisions.choice: both shifts together
decisions.reason: The men coming on duty and those going off duty were both brought to the temple, as Jehoiada had ordered (verses 5-7), so the force was twice its usual size.

decisions.choice: did according to all that he had commanded: full obedience
decisions.reason: The narrator stresses that the plan was carried out exactly as given.

decisions.choice: The commanders
decisions.reason: Readable shortens "commanders of hundreds", already explained at verse 4.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַכֹּהֵ֜ן לְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֗וֹת אֶֽת־הַחֲנִית֙ וְאֶת־הַשְּׁלָטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave the priest to [the] commanders of the hundreds the spear and the shields which [were] to the king David, which [were] in [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And the priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spear and the shields that [had belonged] to King David, which [were] in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The priest handed out to the commanders the spears and shields that had belonged to King David. They were kept in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the spear: spears, a collective
decisions.reason: The word is singular but stands for the spears as a group; 2 Chronicles 23:9 has the plural.

decisions.choice: the shields: probably a kind of shield
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It is used of the gold pieces David took from Hadadezer's officers (2 Samuel 8:7), and was most likely a type of shield, though some take it as quivers or as armor in general.

decisions.choice: David's weapons in the temple: trophies kept at the house of Yahweh
decisions.reason: Weapons won in battle were kept in a sanctuary as a sign of victory (1 Samuel 21:10; 2 Samuel 8:7, 11). Arming the guard with David's own weapons tied the new king to David's line.

decisions.choice: spears
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the collective singular as a plural (m1).

source.text: וַיַּעַמְד֨וּ הָרָצִ֜ים אִ֣ישׁ׀וְכֵלָ֣יו בְּיָד֗וֹ מִכֶּ֨תֶף הַבַּ֤יִת הַיְמָנִית֙ עַד־כֶּ֤תֶף הַבַּ֨יִת֙ הַשְּׂמָאלִ֔ית לַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וְלַבָּ֑יִת עַל־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And stood the runners, each man and his weapons in his hand, from [the] side of the house the right to [the] side of the house the left, by the altar and by the house, by the king all around.

en.L: And the runners stood, each man with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and by the house, around the king on every side.
en.B: The guards took their places, each man with his weapons in hand, from the south side of the temple to the north side, beside the altar and the temple, surrounding the king.
en.R: The guards stood in their places, holding their weapons. They formed a line from the south side of the temple to the north side, near the altar and the temple building, to surround and protect the king.

decisions.choice: right side, left side: south side, north side
decisions.reason: Directions were named facing east, the way the temple faced, so "right" is south and "left" is north. The guards stretched across the whole front of the temple.

decisions.choice: the altar and the house: the open court in front of the temple
decisions.reason: The altar for burnt offerings stood in the court before the temple building (1 Kings 8:64). The guards filled the space between the altar and the building, where the king would be shown.

decisions.choice: around the king: in position to guard him
decisions.reason: The guard took up its places around the spot where the king would stand; he is brought out in the next verse.

decisions.choice: south side; north side
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the compass directions that "right" and "left" mean here (m1).

decisions.choice: to surround and protect the king
decisions.reason: Readable adds "protect" to make the guard's purpose clear (verse 8).

source.text: וַיּוֹצִ֣א אֶת־בֶּן־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיִּתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ אֶת־הַנֵּ֨זֶר֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣עֵד֔וּת וַיַּמְלִ֥כוּ אֹת֖וֹ וַיִּמְשָׁחֻ֑הוּ וַיַּכּוּ־כָ֔ף וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he brought out the son of the king and put on him the crown and the testimony, and they made king him and anointed him, and struck a palm and said, may live the king.

en.L: And he brought out the son of the king and put on him the crown and the testimony; and they made him king and anointed him, and they clapped [their] hands and said, "May the king live!"
en.B: Then Jehoiada brought out the king's son and put on him the crown and the testimony. They made him king and anointed him. Then they clapped their hands and shouted, "Long live the king!"
en.R: Then Jehoiada brought out the king's son. He put the crown on him and the testimony. They made him king and poured olive oil on his head. Everyone clapped and shouted, "Long live the king!"

decisions.choice: the testimony: probably a written copy of Yahweh's covenant law
decisions.reason: The word is used for the covenant law, especially the tablets kept in the ark (Exodus 25:16, 21). The king was to have his own copy of the law (Deuteronomy 17:18-19), and this may be what was given to Joash at his crowning, perhaps placed on him or held over him. Because Saul's crown is paired with an armband in 2 Samuel 1:10, and the two Hebrew words look alike, some think this was a royal ornament rather than a document.

decisions.choice: the crown: the sign of a consecrated ruler
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning "set apart". It names the royal crown (2 Samuel 1:10) and also the high priest's holy diadem (Exodus 29:6).

decisions.choice: may the king live: the acclamation of a new king
decisions.reason: This is the cry with which the people welcomed a new king, as with Saul and Solomon (1 Samuel 10:24; 1 Kings 1:25, 39).

decisions.choice: anointed him and clapped their hands: the public crowning
decisions.reason: Anointing with oil set a man apart as king (1 Kings 1:39). Clapping was a shout of joy and loyalty for a king (Psalm 47:2).

decisions.choice: Long live the king!
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 1:25, Balanced and Readable use the familiar English acclamation; Literal keeps the Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: the testimony
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "testimony", the singular used for the covenant tablets, rather than "decrees" or "instructions" used for the plural, because the sense here is uncertain (m1).

decisions.choice: Jehoiada; poured olive oil on his head
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jehoiada as the one who brought the boy out; Readable explains what anointing is, as in 1 Kings 1:34.

source.text: וַתִּשְׁמַ֣ע עֲתַלְיָ֔ה אֶת־ק֥וֹל הָֽרָצִ֖ין הָעָ֑ם וַתָּבֹ֥א אֶל־הָעָ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Athaliah the sound of the runners, the people, and came to the people [to the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And Athaliah heard the sound of the runners [and] the people, and she came to the people [in] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people, she went to the people at the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Athaliah heard the noise the guards and the people were making. So she went to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, where the people were.

decisions.choice: the runners, the people: the guards and the people
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side with no "and", and "runners" has an unusual ending. The sense is the noise of the guards together with the crowd. 2 Chronicles 23:12 has "the people running and praising the king".

decisions.choice: she came to the people: Athaliah goes into the temple court
decisions.reason: She came alone into the place where the guards had been set (verses 7-11), into the trap that had been laid.

decisions.choice: and
decisions.reason: English needs "and" between the two nouns (m1); Literal brackets it.

source.text: וַתֵּ֡רֶא וְהִנֵּ֣ה הַמֶּלֶךְ֩ עֹמֵ֨ד עַֽל־הָעַמּ֜וּד כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֗ט וְהַשָּׂרִ֤ים וְהַחֲצֹֽצְרוֹת֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכָל־עַ֤ם הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ שָׂמֵ֔חַ וְתֹקֵ֖עַ בַּחֲצֹֽצְר֑וֹת וַתִּקְרַ֤ע עֲתַלְיָה֙ אֶת־בְּגָדֶ֔יהָ וַתִּקְרָ֖א קֶ֥שֶׁר קָֽשֶׁר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And she looked, and look, the king [was] standing by the pillar according to the custom, and the commanders and the trumpets [were] by the king, and all [the] people of the land [were] rejoicing and blowing on trumpets; and tore Athaliah her clothes and called out, conspiracy, conspiracy.

en.L: And she looked, and look, the king [was] standing by the pillar according to the custom, and the commanders and the trumpets [were] beside the king, and all the people of the land [were] rejoicing and blowing on trumpets; and Athaliah tore her clothes and called out, "Treason! Treason!"
en.B: She looked, and there was the king, standing by the pillar as the custom was, with the commanders and the trumpeters beside him. All the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"
en.R: She looked and saw the new king standing by the pillar, where kings stood by custom. The commanders and the trumpet players were next to him. All the people of the land were celebrating and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and screamed, "Treason! Treason!"

decisions.choice: by the pillar according to the custom: the king's place in the temple court
decisions.reason: The king had a set place by a pillar at the temple, where he stood on public occasions (23:3). It may have been one of the two bronze pillars at the entrance (1 Kings 7:21) or a raised platform; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the citizens of Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase here means the free people of Judah as a body, as distinct from the court and the palace. They support Joash and take part in the covenant (verses 17-20).

decisions.choice: treason: a conspiracy against the ruler
decisions.reason: The word means a plot or conspiracy, the same word used of Jehu's plot against Joram (9:14). Repeated, it is a cry of alarm. Athaliah calls the crowning of David's heir a plot against her.

decisions.choice: tore her clothes: a sign of distress
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes showed grief, horror or alarm (2 Kings 5:7; 6:30).

decisions.choice: the commanders and the trumpets: the officers and the trumpeters
decisions.reason: "The trumpets" stands for those who blew them, beside the king.

decisions.choice: the trumpeters (Balanced); the trumpet players (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who stood by the king (m5); Literal keeps "trumpets".

decisions.choice: Treason! Treason!
decisions.reason: "Treason" gives the sense of a plot against the throne in a short cry; "Conspiracy!" would be the more literal word, but is not something one shouts.

source.text: וַיְצַו֩ יְהוֹיָדָ֨ע הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־שָׂרֵ֥י הַמֵּא֣וֹת׀פְּקֻדֵ֣י הַחַ֗יִל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ הוֹצִ֤יאוּ אֹתָהּ֙ אֶל־מִבֵּ֣ית לַשְּׂדֵרֹ֔ת וְהַבָּ֥א אַחֲרֶ֖יהָ הָמֵ֣ת בֶּחָ֑רֶב כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אַל־תּוּמַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded Jehoiada the priest [the] commanders of the hundreds, [the] appointed ones of the army, and said to them, bring out her to from between the ranks, and the [one] coming after her put to death with [the] sword; for had said the priest, not let her be put to death [in the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds, the officers of the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever comes after her, put [him] to death with the sword." For the priest had said, "Let her not be put to death [in] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: Jehoiada the priest gave orders to the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the troops: "Bring her out between the ranks, and kill with the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest had said, "Do not let her be killed in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Jehoiada the priest gave orders to the commanders in charge of the soldiers. He said, "Take her out between your lines, and kill anyone who follows her." He said this because he did not want her killed in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: out between the ranks: out through the lines of guards
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. It most likely means that she is to be led out between the guards' lines (verse 8), under guard. It may also mean "out of the temple precincts".

decisions.choice: whoever comes after her: anyone who follows her to help her
decisions.reason: Anyone who came to her aid was to be treated as an attacker.

decisions.choice: not in the house of Yahweh: the temple must not be defiled by her death
decisions.reason: Killing in the holy place would defile it. The priest's words explain why she was taken out before she was killed (verse 16).

decisions.choice: the appointed ones of the army: the officers in charge of the troops
decisions.reason: The phrase describes the commanders of hundreds; it is not a second group.

decisions.choice: He said this because he did not want her killed
decisions.reason: Readable turns the priest's reported words into a statement of his reason.

source.text: וַיָּשִׂ֤מוּ לָהּ֙ יָדַ֔יִם וַתָּב֛וֹא דֶּֽרֶךְ־מְב֥וֹא הַסּוּסִ֖ים בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַתּוּמַ֖ת שָֽׁם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they put to her hands, and she went [by the] way of [the] entrance of the horses [to the] house of the king, and she was put to death there.

en.L: And they laid hands on her, and she went by the way of the entrance of the horses [to] the house of the king, and she was put to death there.
en.B: They seized her, and she went out by way of the horses' entrance to the king's palace, and there she was put to death.
en.R: So they took hold of her and led her out through the gate where the horses entered the palace grounds. There she was killed.

decisions.choice: they laid hands on her: they seized her
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. It most likely means that the guards took hold of her. It may also mean "they made way for her", letting her pass out between them; 2 Chronicles 23:15 has the same words.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the horses: a gate into the palace grounds
decisions.reason: This was the way horses were brought into the royal grounds, outside the temple court. 2 Chronicles 23:15 calls it "the entrance of the Horse Gate"; Jeremiah 31:40 names a Horse Gate in the city wall.

decisions.choice: the gate where the horses entered
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name of the entrance.

source.text: וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע אֶֽת־הַבְּרִ֗ית בֵּ֤ין יְהוָה֙ וּבֵ֤ין הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָעָ֔ם לִהְי֥וֹת לְעָ֖ם לַֽיהוָ֑ה וּבֵ֥ין הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וּבֵ֥ין הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And cut Jehoiada the covenant between Yahweh and between the king and between the people, to be as a people to Yahweh, and between the king and between the people.

en.L: And Jehoiada made the covenant between {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the king and the people, that they should be a people for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and between the king and the people.
en.B: Jehoiada made the covenant between {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the king and the people, that they would be the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He also made one between the king and the people.
en.R: Then Jehoiada made a covenant that bound {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the king and the people together. The people promised to belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The king and the people also made a covenant with each other.

decisions.choice: the covenant: Israel's covenant with Yahweh renewed
decisions.reason: "The covenant" with the article is the covenant already known, the bond between Yahweh and his people. "To be a people for Yahweh" is its central promise (Exodus 6:7; Deuteronomy 26:18). After Athaliah's years of Baal worship, king and people bind themselves to Yahweh again.

decisions.choice: between the king and the people: a covenant of kingship
decisions.reason: A second agreement set out the duties of king and people to each other, as when the elders of Israel made a covenant with David (2 Samuel 5:3). 2 Chronicles 23:16 has only the first covenant, made "between himself and all the people and the king".

decisions.choice: a covenant that bound the LORD, the king and the people together; The people promised
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the covenant joined all three, and makes the people's promise a sentence of its own.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ כָל־עַם֩ הָאָ֨רֶץ בֵּית־הַבַּ֜עַל וַֽיִּתְּצֻ֗הוּ אֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתָ֤יו וְאֶת־צְלָמָיו֙ שִׁבְּר֣וּ הֵיטֵ֔ב וְאֵ֗ת מַתָּן֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הַבַּ֔עַל הָרְג֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י הַֽמִּזְבְּח֑וֹת וַיָּ֧שֶׂם הַכֹּהֵ֛ן פְּקֻדּ֖וֹת עַל־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went all [the] people of the land [to the] house of the Baal and pulled it down; its altars and its images they broke well, and Mattan, priest of the Baal, they killed before the altars; and put the priest appointed [guards] over [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And all the people of the land went [to] the house of Baal and pulled it down; its altars and its images they broke thoroughly, and Mattan the priest of Baal they killed before the altars. And the priest set appointed [guards] over the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then all the people of the land went to Baal's house and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images to pieces, and killed Mattan, Baal's priest, before the altars. The priest posted guards over the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then all the people of the land went to Baal's temple and tore it down. They smashed its altars and idols to pieces. They killed Mattan, Baal's priest, in front of the altars. Then Jehoiada the priest put guards in charge of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the house of Baal: a temple of Baal in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Baal worship came to Judah through the house of Ahab, to which Athaliah belonged (8:18; 1 Kings 16:31-32). Jehu had already destroyed Baal's temple in Samaria (10:18-28); now the same is done in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: its images: the idols in the temple
decisions.reason: The word means images or statues; here, images of Baal or of the gods worshiped with him.

decisions.choice: Mattan: the priest of Baal
decisions.reason: Mattan is named only here and in 2 Chronicles 23:17. He was killed at his own altars.

decisions.choice: appointed guards: watches set over the temple
decisions.reason: The word means offices or posts of oversight. Jehoiada set guards over the temple of Yahweh, perhaps to protect it from Athaliah's supporters. 2 Chronicles 23:18-19 tells at length how he set the priests, Levites and gatekeepers in order.

decisions.choice: broke thoroughly: smashed to pieces
decisions.reason: The verb with the added word "well" means a complete destruction.

decisions.choice: idols; Jehoiada the priest
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word "idols" and names the priest.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־שָׂרֵ֣י הַ֠מֵּאוֹת וְאֶת־הַכָּרִ֨י וְאֶת־הָרָצִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת׀כָּל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֗רֶץ וַיֹּרִ֤ידוּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּב֛וֹאוּ דֶּֽרֶך־שַׁ֥עַרהָרָצִ֖ים בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב עַל־כִּסֵּ֥א הַמְּלָכִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took [the] commanders of the hundreds and the Carites and the runners and all [the] people of the land, and they brought down the king from [the] house of Yahweh and came [by the] way of [the] gate of the runners [to the] house of the king; and he sat on [the] throne of the kings.

en.L: And he took the commanders of hundreds and the Carites and the runners and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they came by the way of the gate of the runners [to] the house of the king; and he sat on the throne of the kings.
en.B: He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards and all the people of the land. They escorted the king down from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and went by way of the gate of the guards to the king's palace. And the king took his seat on the royal throne.
en.R: Jehoiada gathered the commanders, the Carites, the guards and all the people of the land. Together they led the king down from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They went through the gate of the guards into the palace, and the king sat down on the royal throne.

decisions.choice: brought the king down from the house of Yahweh: from the temple hill to the palace
decisions.reason: The temple stood on higher ground than the palace, so going from one to the other was going down.

decisions.choice: the gate of the runners: the guards' gate into the palace
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, where it is called "the gate behind the runners".

decisions.choice: the throne of the kings: the throne of David's line
decisions.reason: The throne on which the kings of Judah had sat now has a king of David's line again.

decisions.choice: the Carites
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

decisions.choice: the king took his seat on the royal throne
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the king as the one who sat, and say "royal throne" for "throne of the kings".

source.text: וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח כָּל־עַם־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהָעִ֣יר שָׁקָ֑טָה וְאֶת־עֲתַלְיָ֛הוּ הֵמִ֥יתוּ בַחֶ֖רֶב בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And rejoiced all [the] people of the land, and the city was quiet; and Athaliah they had put to death with the sword [at the] house of [the] king.

en.L: And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and Athaliah they had put to death with the sword [at] the house of the king.
en.B: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was at peace. Athaliah had been put to death with the sword at the king's palace.
en.R: All the people of the land were happy, and the city was calm. Athaliah had been killed with a sword at the palace.

decisions.choice: the people rejoiced and the city was quiet
decisions.reason: Two pictures stand side by side: the people of Judah celebrate, and Jerusalem stays quiet, with no one rising to fight for Athaliah.

decisions.choice: Athaliah they had put to death: the story closes on her end
decisions.reason: The verb looks back to verse 16. Putting Athaliah's name first closes the story where it began (verse 1).

decisions.choice: the house of the king
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "a king's house" and the traditional reading notes "the king's house"; the sense is the same.
